practiceReport.name: Kyren Williams
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Listed as a limited participant on the Rams' initial Week 12 injury report posted Sunday, Williams quelled any concern about his status for Wednesday's game against the Packers by taking full reps a day later. Though his sore toe isn't expected to affect his workload, Williams nonetheless may find himself in a timeshare with Blake Corum, who has been the more productive option on the ground this season. Williams has totaled seven touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards per carry through 10 games, while Corum has scored six times and is averaging 5.3 yards per tote.

practiceReport.name: Davis Allen
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

practiceReport.name: Colby Parkinson
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
practiceReport.beatComment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

practiceReport.beatComment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Terrance Ferguson
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 11 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Davante Adams
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Puka Nacua
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.
